subject: chemistry
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Alkenes are described as unsaturated because they contain:
questions.explain: Alkenes are unsaturated because they contain at least one C=C double bond.

questions.q: Potassium ions produce which colour in a flame test?
questions.explain: Potassium ions give a lilac flame colour.

questions.q: Adding sodium hydroxide to iron(III) ions produces a precipitate that is:
questions.explain: Iron(III) ions give a brown precipitate of iron(III) hydroxide.

questions.q: Crude oil is a mixture made mostly of which type of compound?
questions.explain: Crude oil is a mixture of hydrocarbons, most of which are alkanes.

questions.q: In a flame test, lithium ions give which colour?
questions.explain: Lithium ions produce a crimson flame.

questions.q: Reducing, reusing and recycling materials is important because it:
options: Conserves finite resources and limited energy
questions.explain: Recycling conserves finite resources and uses less energy than making materials from scratch.

questions.q: Which statement about alkanes is correct?
options: They are unsaturated and decolourise bromine water
They are saturated and do not decolourise bromine water
They all contain a C=C bond
questions.explain: Alkanes are saturated, with only single bonds, so they do not decolourise bromine water.

questions.q: Poly(ethene) is made from ethene molecules by:
questions.explain: Many ethene (alkene) monomers join in addition polymerisation to form poly(ethene).

questions.q: In treating potable water from fresh sources, sterilisation is used to:
questions.explain: Sterilisation, for example with chlorine, kills harmful microbes in drinking water.

questions.q: A possible consequence of climate change caused by rising greenhouse gases is:
questions.explain: Increased greenhouse gases raise global temperatures, leading to more extreme weather.

questions.q: How can you test for the presence of carbonate ions?
options: Add silver nitrate to form a precipitate
Add acid and bubble the gas through limewater
questions.explain: Carbonates react with acid to release carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky.

questions.q: In paper chromatography, the Rf value is calculated as:
options: Distance moved by solvent / distance moved by substance
Distance moved by substance / distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by substance x distance moved by solvent
Distance moved by solvent - distance moved by substance
questions.explain: Rf = distance moved by the substance divided by the distance moved by the solvent.

questions.q: Which test confirms that a gas is hydrogen?
options: It gives a squeaky pop with a lit splint
questions.explain: Hydrogen produces a squeaky pop when a lit splint is held to it.

questions.q: A white precipitate forms when barium chloride is added to a solution containing:
questions.explain: Sulfate ions form a white precipitate of barium sulfate with barium chloride.

questions.q: A substance that does not move from the baseline in chromatography is most likely:
questions.explain: A spot that stays on the baseline is insoluble in that solvent and does not travel.

questions.q: When silver nitrate is added to a solution containing iodide ions, the precipitate is:
questions.explain: Iodide ions form a yellow precipitate of silver iodide.

questions.q: Crude oil is separated into fractions by fractional distillation according to differences in:
questions.explain: Fractional distillation separates the hydrocarbons by their different boiling points.

questions.q: Cracking of long-chain hydrocarbons usually requires:
options: A high temperature and a catalyst (or steam)
questions.explain: Cracking uses high temperatures with a catalyst, or high temperatures and steam.

questions.q: Which technique would best separate two coloured dyes in an ink?
questions.explain: Chromatography separates a mixture of soluble coloured substances by how far each travels.

questions.q: Acid rain damages the environment by:
options: Killing trees and aquatic life and eroding stonework
questions.explain: Acid rain harms trees, fish and lakes and corrodes buildings made of limestone.

questions.q: Which flame colour indicates the presence of sodium ions?
questions.explain: Sodium ions produce a yellow flame in a flame test.

questions.q: Why is carbon monoxide especially dangerous to humans?
options: It is colourless and odourless and reduces oxygen carried by the blood
questions.explain: Carbon monoxide is toxic because it is hard to detect and stops blood carrying oxygen.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel GCSE (9–1) Chemistry (1CH0) specification; Separate Chemistry 2
